name: Hang Bac
kicker: Guild street of silver in the Old Quarter
summary: Hang Bac is the silver street, one of the 36 guild streets still named for its trade. You walk past jewellers’ windows lit gold under signs for vàng bạc, gold and silver, with silver-engraving shops and breakfast stools in between. Walk it as part of the Old Quarter loop from the lake rather than as a separate trip.
getThere: Walk the lanes north of Hoan Kiem Lake
heroCaption: Jewellers’ windows and gold-and-silver signs on Hang Bac
body: The Old Quarter’s streets have been named for the goods their artisans made since the 14th or 15th century, and Hang Bac’s is silver. The shopfronts still show it: glass counters of jewellery, signs reading vàng bạc and đá quý, and house numbers painted on every board.

Between the jewellers are silver-engraving workshops and the street kitchens of the lanes, with plastic stools on the pavement in the morning. Walk it slowly, look in the windows, and keep it on the same loop as Bach Ma and Dong Xuan.

figures.caption: A silver-engraving shop at 100 Hang Bac, with breakfast stools out front
figures.alt: A shopfront signed for silver engraving at 100 Hàng Bạc, with people on plastic stools outside

gettingThere: Hang Bac is one of the guild streets in the lanes north of Hoan Kiem Lake. Walk north from the lake into the quarter; it is free to walk.
